name: to_csv
description: Write a JSON array of objects as CSV, for a file, a report or a spreadsheet. The columns come from the first row unless you name them. A nested value is refused rather than rendered, and a column that only later rows carry is refused rather than dropped.

data.description: The JSON array to write, usually a step's result: "{{ steps.rows.text }}". Pass this or path, not both.

path.description: A JSON file to read instead, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside it. Pass this or data, not both.

columns.description: Which fields become columns, and in which order. Without this they are the keys of the first row, and a row carrying a key the first row does not is refused. Naming them also lets a row leave one out, which becomes an empty cell.

header.description: Whether to write the column names as the first line. Set false when appending to a file that already has one.

delimiter.description: The field separator, one character. A tab is written "\t".

output_schema.description: CSV, one line per row, ending in a newline. A cell is quoted only when it holds the delimiter, a quote or a line break, so the common case stays readable. A quote inside a quoted cell is doubled. null is an empty cell; a number or a boolean is written the way JSON writes it.

exit_codes.2: invalid input (stdin was not a JSON object, or a parameter is missing or the wrong type)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (path resolves outside the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: malformed data (the data is not JSON, or not an array of objects)
exit_codes.6: refused (a value is nested, a row carries a column the first row does not, or the array is empty and no columns were named)
